purpose: Separate operational metrics from public metrics and define the minimum sample, cohort-maturity, freshness and scope conditions required before BetterMakati publishes rates or timing summaries.
implementationBoundary: No dashboard, API, analytics event, contributor identifier, aggregate endpoint or UI threshold enforcement is added in W3R-10b.
principles: Exact public records may exist before an aggregate is suitable for headline publication.
Small denominators may be shown as counts, but they must not be converted into representative-looking percentages merely because a percentage is mathematically possible.
A publication threshold is a display guardrail, not a service-level agreement, performance target or statistical claim of representativeness.
Recent case cohorts must mature before later-stage outcome rates are published.
Public timing summaries use medians rather than averages because a few long-running cases can distort a mean.
No metric may collapse BetterMakati referral, government acknowledgement, action evidence and documented resolution into one response measure.
Audit coverage is a census of a frozen campaign target set, not a population estimate; its scope must remain visible.
Observation freshness describes recency of evidence, not quality of a place.
Repeat-contributor metrics remain operational/internal in Wave 3 even after privacy-safe instrumentation exists.
When a public threshold is not met, show the underlying factual state or an insufficient-data label rather than 0%.

publicationClasses.public-now: May be displayed publicly when its metric-specific evidence and context requirements are satisfied; no minimum-volume rate threshold is required.
publicationClasses.public-after-threshold: May be displayed publicly only when all metric-specific volume, maturity and evidence requirements are satisfied.
publicationClasses.internal-only: May be computed for operations/QA but must not be used as a public headline metric in Wave 3.
publicationClasses.not-yet-measurable: Must not be calculated from current data because required instrumentation or a privacy-safe identity basis does not exist.

globalRules.zeroDenominator: Display not applicable / no eligible records, never 0%.
globalRules.durationCompanion: Show event count; interquartile range may be shown when at least 20 stage events exist.
globalRules.percentagePrecision: Whole percentages by default. Do not add decimal precision to small civic datasets.
globalRules.countsBelowRateThreshold: Exact numerator and denominator counts may still be shown when useful, but omit the percentage and explain that the cohort is below the publication threshold.
globalRules.comparisons: Do not compare periods, barangays, place categories or campaigns using a rate unless every compared group independently meets the same publication threshold and uses an equivalent definition.
globalRules.trendRule: Do not label an increase/decrease as a trend unless at least three consecutive comparable published windows meet all thresholds.

barangayBreakdown.rule: Barangay-level counts can remain visible as factual case records, but rates/timing summaries are suppressed below these thresholds. Free-text barangay mentions never establish the denominator.

globalRules.noRanking: Threshold-passing metrics still may not be turned into best/worst barangay, place, authority or contributor rankings.

caseLifecycle.cohortDefinition: Eligible civic cases grouped by case createdAt in the selected reporting window.
caseLifecycle.maturityBasis: A cohort is mature for a stage only when asOf is at least the stage's maturityDays after the cohort end.

rateRules.belowThresholdFallback: Show submitted and reviewed counts only.
Show submitted and routed counts only.
rateRules.wordingGuardrail: Never relabel routed as received, acknowledged or accepted by government.

rateRules.requiredEvidence: acknowledged civic-admin event with a non-empty authority/responsible-body field
rateRules.belowThresholdFallback: Show the count of cases with documented authority acknowledgement only.
Show the count of cases with action evidence only.
rateRules.wordingGuardrail: Do not describe action evidence as resolution.
Do not use GitHub closed state or ordinary appears-resolved comments as the numerator.

internalDiagnostics.reason: This is a workflow-quality diagnostic for whether forwarded events identify destination/channel, not a civic outcome.
Used to detect inconsistent lifecycle recording such as acknowledgement predating routing.

entityLevelLatestObservation.display: Show the actual latest observedAt date or age together with sample count. Do not hide old observations; old evidence remains useful when clearly dated.

observationFreshness.freshnessLabelRule: An entity may be described as having a recent observation only when its latest observedAt is within the family-specific window. Beyond the window, show the date/age without calling the place stale, poor or noncompliant.

aggregateFreshnessCoverage.numerator: Eligible entities whose latest observation falls within the applicable recent-observation window.
aggregateFreshnessCoverage.denominator: Explicit eligible entity set for the published scope.
aggregateFreshnessCoverage.scopeGuardrail: Do not publish a citywide freshness percentage from a partial inventory.

civicAuditCoverage.whyNoMinimumSampleRate: The denominator is the campaign's complete frozen target set, so coverage is a census of that declared campaign scope rather than an estimate from a sample.
requirements: Every target ID resolves to the declared entity kind.
Campaign period and asOf are shown.
Inventory claim and scope statement are shown.
Numerator and denominator counts are displayed with any percentage.
Entities with zero qualifying observations remain visible.
Live campaigns are labeled in progress / as of the displayed timestamp.
Ended campaigns distinguish period ended from target fully covered.

smallTargetPresentation.rule: Show x of y coverage as the primary display; percentage may appear secondarily but must not be used as a headline by itself.

civicAuditCoverage.questionDistributionBoundary: Question-level condition distributions remain governed by the civic-audit campaign schema and must always show sample counts. They are not converted into place scores or rankings by this metric policy.

instrumentationPrerequisites: Key is not derived from IP address, public alias or free-text name.
Retention and deletion rules are documented.
repeatContribution.publicRule: Do not publish repeat-contributor rates, contributor leaderboards or contributor-level histories in Wave 3. The metric may be used internally after its privacy prerequisites are satisfied.

publicPresentationMatrix.condition: Exact source-backed counts with explicit period/cohort and lifecycle label.
At least 20 eligible cases and the stage-specific cohort maturity period has elapsed.
At least 10 observed stage events and the stage-specific maturity period has elapsed.
At least one valid structured observation; always show sample count.
Explicit eligible inventory of at least 10 entities, at least 5 with observations, and a declared family-specific freshness window.
Frozen target set, campaign period/asOf, inventory claim and x/y counts are visible.
Privacy prerequisites satisfied; never a public Wave 3 headline.

suppressionLabels.smallCohort: Not enough cases for a stable public rate yet
suppressionLabels.immatureCohort: Cohort is still too recent for this outcome rate
suppressionLabels.insufficientStageEvents: Not enough completed stage events for a timing summary yet
suppressionLabels.partialInventory: Coverage percentage withheld because the eligible inventory is incomplete
suppressionLabels.notMeasurable: Not currently measurable with privacy-safe data

nextStep.title: Instrument redesigned participation outcomes
nextStep.scope: API/data instrumentation only for fields defined in W3R-10a/10b. No headline aggregates.
